dishes.name: Boeuf bourguignon
dishes.desc: Charolais beef stewed slowly in red Burgundy wine with onions, bacon and mushrooms. Burgundy's festive and Sunday dish, found on nearly every traditional menu.

dishes.name: Oeufs en meurette
dishes.desc: Eggs poached directly in a dark red-wine sauce with bacon and onions, served on toast. A Burgundy starter that Dijon kitchens treat as a classic.

dishes.name: Jambon persillé
dishes.desc: Shoulder ham cooked for hours in a strong stock, then set in parsley aspic and sliced cold. A Burgundian dish traditionally linked to Easter.

dishes.name: Burgundy snails
dishes.desc: Snails baked in their shells with garlic and parsley butter. Burgundy's most famous starter, served in Dijon's traditional restaurants.

dishes.name: Pain d'épices de Dijon
dishes.desc: Dense honey-spice cake that has been part of Dijon since the French Revolution era. Traditionally eaten toasted and buttered at breakfast.

dishes.name: Époisses
dishes.desc: Strong, soft cow's-milk cheese with an orange rind washed in the local spirit. A Burgundy classic eaten at the end of a meal.

dishes.name: Gougères
dishes.desc: Small choux-pastry puffs baked with cheese, a Burgundian speciality. Served warm at the aperitif and sold in bakeries.
